Oily.description: Oily skin is characterized by the overproduction of sebum (seborrhea), often genetic or hormonal. This leads to comedones and provides a fertile environment for C. acnes bacteria.
sideEffects: Enlarged pores, greasy texture, and shiny look.
Frequent acne breakouts, blackheads, and whiteheads.
Makeup does not stay in place for long.
Susceptibility to fungal acne (Malassezia folliculitis).
avoid: Heavy oil based creams and thick makeup products.
Over cleansing (triggers rebound oil production).
Skipping moisturizer (can lead to dehydration and more oil).
Sugary and fried foods that may increase sebum production.
tips: Use gentle gel based or foaming cleansers.
Opt for oil free, lightweight moisturizers.
Use blotting paper to manage shine during the day.
Incorporate BHA (Salicylic Acid) liquid exfoliant 3 times a week.
Apply clay or charcoal masks 1–2 times weekly.
Use a matte finish, non comedogenic sunscreen daily.
recommendedIngredients: Niacinamide (reduces oil and pore size).
Salicylic Acid (BHA) (penetrates deep to dissolve sebum).
Retinoids (Vitamin A derivatives that regulate sebum and cell turnover).
Zinc PCA, Green Tea Extract, Clay Minerals.

Dry.description: Dry skin (xerosis) involves a lack of both moisture and sebum, leading to a compromised skin barrier and increased Transepidermal Water Loss (TEWL).
sideEffects: Tight feeling, rough texture, and flaky/scaly patches.
Dull appearance due to dehydration.
Fine lines appear more visible.
Prone to irritation, itching, and cracking.
avoid: Hot water while washing the face or bathing.
Foaming cleansers containing sulfates.
Alcohol based products and astringent toners.
Using heating/cooling systems that excessively dry the air.
tips: Use a hydrating cream based cleanser with ceramides.
Moisturize immediately after cleansing while skin is damp.
Use thicker creams or ointments at night (occlusives).
Run a humidifier in dry climates.
Exfoliate very gently (once a week maximum).
recommendedIngredients: Hyaluronic Acid (HA) (draws and binds water).
Ceramides (repairs skin barrier and prevents water loss).
Shea Butter / Squalane (occlusives to lock in moisture).
Glycerin, Urea, Lactic Acid (mild AHA for hydration).

Combination.description: Combination skin exhibits distinct zonal characteristics: typically oiliness in the T zone (forehead, nose, and chin) and dryness or normality on the cheeks and jawline.
sideEffects: Oily forehead and nose, but dry/normal cheeks.
Frequent blackheads on the T zone.
Difficulty choosing the correct moisturizer consistency.
Occasional acne breakouts and flakiness together.
avoid: Using one uniform product for the entire face.
Heavy creams on oily zones.
Skipping moisturizer on dry areas.
Harsh physical scrubs or alcohol based toners.
tips: Use a gentle, pH balanced cleanser.
Apply lightweight gel moisturizer all over the face.
Use multi masking (clay mask on T zone, hydrating mask on cheeks).
Balance routine with Niacinamide or Panthenol.
Employ 'zonal moisturizing' by layering a light cream on the cheeks only.
recommendedIngredients: Niacinamide (balances oil and improves barrier).
Hyaluronic Acid (provides lightweight, oil free hydration).
Green Tea, Panthenol (restores balance and soothes).
Mandelic Acid (gentle AHA for exfoliation).

Sensitive.description: Sensitive skin is characterized by an exaggerated inflammatory response to stimuli due to a compromised skin barrier or easily excitable nerve endings. Often linked to Rosacea or Eczema.
sideEffects: Burning, stinging, and redness (Erythema).
Itching and inflamed patches.
Exaggerated reaction to temperature changes (flushing).
Bumpy texture or hives (contact dermatitis) after product use.
avoid: High Risk Irritants (Alcohol denat, Synthetic fragrances, Dyes).
Strong acids or abrasive physical scrubs.
Hot environments (saunas, very hot water).
Frequent product switching or mechanical cleansing brushes.
tips: Always patch test new products.
Adopt a simple 'cleanse, soothe, protect' routine.
Use a low pH, creamy, non foaming cleanser.
Protect from sun with **Mineral Sunscreens** (Zinc Oxide or Titanium Dioxide).
Use cool compresses for flare ups.
Introduce new ingredients one at a time.
recommendedIngredients: Centella Asiatica (Cica) (calms inflammation and repairs barrier).
Ceramides (crucial for lipid replenishment).
Aloe Vera, Colloidal Oatmeal (relieves itching and irritation).
Allantoin, Bisabolol, Squalane.

Normal.description: Normal skin (eudermic) is characterized by optimal balance. Oil and moisture levels are adequate, the barrier function is strong, and the skin is rarely reactive or troubled.
sideEffects: Generally clear of major issues.
Occasional dryness in winter or mild oiliness in summer.
Minor breakouts possible under stress.
Requires preventative care against environmental damage and aging.
avoid: Skipping daily sunscreen or moisturizer.
Over exfoliating healthy skin.
Using harsh or heavily fragranced products unnecessarily.
Using products designed for severe acne or oil control.
tips: Maintain a consistent cleanse, treat, moisturize, and SPF routine.
Incorporate a **Vitamin C serum** in the morning for protection.
Introduce a mild **Retinoid** (retinol/retinaldehyde) at night for prevention.
Use a mild **chemical exfoliator** 1–2 times per week.
Focus on neck and chest care as well.
recommendedIngredients: Vitamin C (antioxidant that fights free radical damage).
Retinoids (boost cell turnover and stimulate collagen).
Hyaluronic Acid (maintains healthy hydration levels).
Peptides (signal the skin to produce more collagen).
Niacinamide, Vitamin E, Resveratrol.
